author: /root/core_review
objective: Finite sorting acceptance Domain and worker instrumentation; no Core changes

baseline.classification: new application-level mechanisms; no historical Core defect claimed

runs.command: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=src:. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_acceptance_sorting.py --tb=short

PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 - <<'PY'
import ast,hashlib,json,pathlib,subprocess
paths=["examples/acceptance/sorting.py","tests/test_acceptance_sorting.py"]
for path in paths:ast.parse(pathlib.Path(path).read_bytes())
tests=ast.parse(pathlib.Path(paths[1]).read_bytes())
changed_src=subprocess.check_output(["git","diff","8f61ae5f68c0846d5149aceb4df55c69263c9df2","--name-only","--","src"],text=True).splitlines()
oldtests=set(subprocess.check_output(["git","ls-tree","-r","--name-only","8f61ae5f68c0846d5149aceb4df55c69263c9df2","tests"],text=True).splitlines())
changedtests=set(subprocess.check_output(["git","diff","8f61ae5f68c0846d5149aceb4df55c69263c9df2","--name-only","--","tests"],text=True).splitlines())
assert not changed_src
assert not oldtests&changedtests
print(json.dumps({"files":[{"path":p,"sha256":hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),"bytes":pathlib.Path(p).stat().st_size} for p in paths],
 "literal_asserts":sum(isinstance(n,ast.Assert) for n in ast.walk(tests)),
 "core_src_changed":[],"old_tests_changed":sorted(oldtests&changedtests),"exit":0},sort_keys=True))
PY

metric.unit: executed value-comparator calls, including comparisons returning False
metric.implementation: Insertion baseline and unchecked selection sort increment cost by appending each actual operand/relation/result trace event; challenger returns the input unchanged and executes zero value comparisons.
metric.independent_checks: Trace checker replays insertion with saved-pivot shifts rather than measured adjacent exchanges, verifies every exact typed event and output; independent Counter multiplicity and adjacent-order oracle evaluates finite-suite correctness.
metric.scope: Only the pinned finite dataset. No universal algorithm-correctness or asymptotic-performance claim.

scientific_semantics.unchecked_measurement: Trace/output instrumentation is checked, but the scientific multiset/order oracle is deliberately not called; a direct tripwire test enforces this boundary.
scientific_semantics.analysis: A later unchecked analyze action reads all three original result artifacts through source FDs, revalidates their data and traces, applies the finite oracle and emits a new valid, higher-cost result. It does not rerun selection sort or mutate the original unknown artifact/claim.
scientific_semantics.independence: Distinct provenance-bound analysis artifact/observation is not a new algorithm measurement or statistically independent repeat.

real_operations: sealed memfd inputs and three source byte streams
fd_unit_boundary.fixture_origins: The three source results are golden unit fixtures produced from actual sorting measurement and shared write_result in the pytest process. They are not claimed to be three prior CLI/native executions.
controls: analysis measure() tripwire proves no algorithm rerun
tampered source descriptor bytes are rejected
three original source objects and unknown interpretation remain unchanged

coverage: Default and counterfactual three-candidate costs and statuses
False-inclusive handwritten insertion and selection traces
Empty rows, negatives, duplicates, and finite multiset/order oracle
Forged count, operand, boolean, early trace termination and output rejected
Three real sealed source FDs and source checksum corruption
Missing sources, duplicate candidate, wrong dataset and bad source trace rejected
Detached and strictly typed dataset configuration
limitations: No Core src file or pre-existing test was changed.
No GPU/provider/network or host process discovery was used.
The 22-case author run is not the root actual-CLI acceptance run or final full-suite evidence.
No initial API absence or manually inferred expected failure is reported as a historical red.
